referents.why: 'your hand' belongs to the one the quoted command is addressed to, Aaron.
'your staff' belongs to Aaron, the addressee of the quoted command.
'say to Aaron' is the LORD's command to Moses, the addressee of cl0. The builder's w7 is the wrong person.
referents.category: implied subject of a command to the speech's addressee

referents.why: 'stretch out your hand' is the message Moses is to tell Aaron, so the implied 'you' is Aaron.
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: 'bring up the frogs' is in the same quoted message, addressed to Aaron.
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

links.why: two commands joined by a plain waw; the second is not a purpose or result (not third person), so 'and' stands.
'he said to Moses' introduces the command 'say to Aaron'.
'tell Aaron' introduces a collection of two commands joined by 'and', so its content is the whole imperative group.

groups.why: the LORD speaks to Moses; the commanded speech of Moses is the part. The builder had the commands as direct parts.
groups.category: outer turn with commanded turn as part

groups.why: Moses is commanded to tell Aaron, so Moses is the one who speaks to Aaron; the builder's sender cl1s is a slot, not a candidate, so it is corrected to Moses.
groups.category: commanded speech spoken by the one commanded

groups.why: the words Moses is to deliver are quoted from the LORD: the innermost turn, whose sender is the one quoted.
'stretch out' and 'bring up' are two commands joined by one waw; 'part' is not an imperative role.
